title: Data loading with explicit states
summary: Load remote data once and expose loading, error, and success states.

scenario.briefing: The product list flickers and keeps a request alive after the page closes. Load the data once, expose each state, and cancel the request on cleanup.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: Move the request into a useEffect with an empty dependency array.
Create an AbortController inside the effect and pass its signal to fetch.
Track loading and error with separate state values.
Return a cleanup function that calls controller.abort().

misconceptions.feedback: Render must stay pure. Start the request in an effect and store the result in state.
misconceptions.testDescription: The effect loads once and aborts on cleanup.

misconceptions.description: Updating state after the component is gone.
misconceptions.feedback: Cancel the request or guard the update so a stale response cannot write state.
misconceptions.diagnostic: A response can resolve after unmount and call setState on a component that no longer exists.

misconceptions.description: Returning only products and hiding loading and error.
misconceptions.feedback: A request has several states. The interface cannot explain failure or show progress without them.
misconceptions.testDescription: The hook exposes products, loading, and error state.

misconceptions.description: Shipping a data component without cancellation or error states.
misconceptions.feedback: Fetching during render, missing keys, missing cancellation, and a missing error state are functional defects. Block the change.

sections.title: Remote data has states
sections.body: A request is not a value. The interface must distinguish loading, failure, empty results, and success.

sections.title: Effects synchronize with the outside world
sections.body: An effect should declare its dependencies and clean up what it started. Cancellation prevents an old response from updating a screen that no longer exists.

sections.title: Errors are data too
sections.body: A failed request should become an error state that the interface can render, not an unhandled rejection.

sections.title: Lists need stable identity
sections.body: When the loaded products are rendered, each item needs a stable key such as product.id so React can preserve the right DOM nodes when the list changes.

vocabulary.definition: A controlled synchronization with an external system.
A browser API for cancelling an in-flight request.
A stale response overwriting newer state.
A stable identity used to match list items across renders.

steps.title: Load products with cancellation
steps.prompt: Edit useProducts.ts. Load products once, expose loading and error state, and cancel the request when the effect cleans up.

tests.description: The hook exposes products, loading, and error state.
The effect loads once and aborts on cleanup.
A failed response sets an error instead of being swallowed.

hints: Keep products state and add loading and error state next to it.
Start the request inside useEffect with an empty dependency array.
Create an AbortController, pass its signal to fetch, and return a cleanup that aborts.
Check response.ok, set an error message in catch, and clear loading in finally.

steps.prompt: Review the artifact and select every real problem.

artifact.title: ProductList.tsx
artifact.caption: The component fetches on every render and writes state without an error or loading path.

findings.label: The fetch call runs during every render.
Each list item lacks a stable key.
A failed request leaves no error state for the user.
There is no cancellation or unmount guard.
The component shows a loading state while the request is pending.

verdicts.label: Block the change until fetching, cancellation, keys, and error handling are fixed.
Ship it; the duplicated requests are harmless.

steps.explanation: Fetching during render repeats work and can update after unmount. The list also lacks stable keys, and a failed request has no error state or loading state to show.
hints: Check where the fetch call runs in the component lifecycle.
Look for a key on each rendered list item.
Look for loading, error, and cancellation paths.
Treat the missing pieces as blockers, not style issues.
